- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior 14-day high.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., -0.4 → +0.1), model frequently underreacts; add 1–2% to forecast to capture sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true price drops when sentiment is negative and price is falling; adjust downward by 1–3% for each -0.10 sentiment unit.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 14-day moving average is above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with trend correction.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.25 or more), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
